results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain include [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [[Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), as well as alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which can be further subdivided into subtypes such as core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, and dorsal. This information comes from VFB. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") records of subclasses of Kenyon cell, indicating that there are multiple types of Kenyon cells. Additionally, VFB has annotated scRNAseq data for Kenyon cell, which may provide further insights into the types of Kenyon cells. To explore the different types of Kenyon cells in more detail, you can use VFB to list all available images of Kenyon cell or to examine the downstream and upstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") is connected to various brain regions, including the mushroom body and lateral horn, through tracts and nerves such as the [adult antenno-subesophageal tract](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007354 "Open adult antenno-subesophageal tract in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult medial antennal lobe tract](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003985 "Open adult medial antennal lobe tract in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [antennal nerve](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00006045 "Open antennal nerve in Virtual Fly Brain"). Specifically, antennal lobe projection neurons send synaptic output to the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn. VFB holds data on tracts and nerves innervating the antennal lobe, with [32](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,TractsNervesInnervatingHere "Run in VFB: Tracts/nerves innervating antennal lobe") records available, as well as neurons with some part in the antennal lobe, including those with synaptic terminals, presynaptic terminals, and postsynaptic terminals. This information comes from the VFB database, which summarizes region connections. To explore the connections of the antennal lobe in more detail, you can examine the available images of the antennal lobe, or investigate the neurons with some part in the antennal lobe, of which VFB has annotated [676](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe") records.

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response:
To address the question regarding the main components of the Drosophila central complex and their associated functions, we must consider the available data and literature. 

The Drosophila central complex is a critical structure in the insect brain, involved in various functions including navigation, locomotion, and spatial memory. It is composed of several distinct substructures, each with specific roles. 

VFB does not currently hold comprehensive data on the detailed composition and functions of the Drosophila central complex. However, based on general knowledge and studies in the field, the central complex is known to include components such as the ellipsoid body, the noduli, the protocerebral bridge, and the fan-shaped body, among others. These components are thought to be involved in integrating sensory information, controlling movement, and facilitating spatial orientation and memory.

For detailed and specific information regarding the functions and components of the Drosophila central complex, consulting the latest research publications and databases such as FlyBase or specific neuroscience literature would be advisable. 

Given the absence of direct evidence in the provided EVIDENCE (JSON) and the lack of specific data in VFB regarding this query, a narrower follow-up into recent studies and databases is recommended to obtain a comprehensive understanding of the Drosophila central complex.

results.title: Bidirectional connectivity
results.question: Are there reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs)? Which pairs have the strongest mutual connectivity?
results.response:
The connectome data indicates that there are reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons. VFB records show 22 reciprocal class-level pairs between these two neuron types. The direction from [dopaminergic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005131 "Open dopaminergic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") to [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") has a partner count of 77, while the direction from mushroom body output neuron to dopaminergic neuron has a partner count of 94. The target-to-source weight is 7620 and the source-to-target weight is 2697. 

To find the pairs with the strongest mutual connectivity, you can explore the top_partners listed in the VFB findings. VFB has annotated a large number of connectivity classes for both mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons, with [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") downstream and [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") upstream connectivity classes for mushroom body output neurons, and [8845](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") downstream and [7914](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") upstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neurons. 

You can further investigate the specific connections and strengths by querying the VFB database for the top_partners and their corresponding weights.

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response:
The pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain") involves intermediate neurons. According to VFB, antennal lobe projection neurons are intermediate neurons that connect olfactory receptor neurons to the adult lateral horn. The high-level pathway is described as: [olfactory receptor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005926 "Open olfactory receptor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> adult lateral horn.

VFB holds various data related to olfactory receptor neurons and the adult lateral horn, including downstream and upstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neurons, and neurons with some part in, or synaptic terminals in, the adult lateral horn. Specifically, VFB has annotated [575](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron") downstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neurons and [379](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron") upstream connectivity classes. For the adult lateral horn, VFB records show [1661](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult lateral horn") neurons with some part in this region and [1658](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in adult lateral horn") neurons with synaptic terminals. 

To further explore the specific intermediate neuron types and their connections, one could examine the available data on neurons with presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals in the adult lateral horn, as well as the tracts/nerves innervating this region, which VFB has also annotated.

results.title: Shared connectivity
results.question: Do the alpha/beta and gamma Kenyon cells converge on any of the same downstream MBON types? Which MBONs receive input from both?
results.response: The connectome data indicates that alpha/beta Kenyon cells and gamma Kenyon cells converge on the same downstream [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") types. VFB records show that some mushroom body output neurons receive input from both alpha/beta and gamma Kenyon cells. Specifically, VFB found 13 shared downstream target classes among the compared source classes, including mushroom body output neuron 32 and mushroom body output neuron 29. VFB has annotated downstream connectivity classes for alpha/beta Kenyon cells ([366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100248,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for KCab") records) and gamma Kenyon cells (data not explicitly provided but available for query), as well as upstream connectivity classes for mushroom body output neurons ([2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") records), which may provide further insight into the convergence of these cell types. To explore the specific mushroom body output neurons that receive input from both alpha/beta and gamma Kenyon cells, you can query the downstream connectivity classes for these cell types.

results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response:
The anatomical containment hierarchy from the [antennal lobe glomerulus DA1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003932 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 in Virtual Fly Brain") up to the top-level brain structure, as recorded in VFB, is: antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. This information is based on the VFB trace containment chain data. 

VFB holds various records related to the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, including neurons with some part in it, neurons with synaptic terminals in it, images of neurons with some part in it, and transgene expression data. Specifically, VFB has annotated [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, 10 neurons with synaptic terminals in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") neurons with presynaptic terminals in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, and [8](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") neurons with postsynaptic terminals in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1. Additionally, there are [911](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 and [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") records of transgene expression in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1. 

To further explore the hierarchy and related data, you can query VFB for more information on the adult antennal lobe, adult deutocerebrum, adult cerebrum, adult central brain, and adult brain, as well as investigate the neurons and images associated with the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1.

results.title: Cross-region connectivity
results.question: What neuron types connect the central complex to the lateral accessory lobe, and how strong are these connections?
results.response: The connectome data indicates that several neuron types connect the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003632 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") to the [lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00050314 "Open lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018 in Virtual Fly Brain"), including PFL1, PFL2_PB4, and PFL3_PB7. VFB records show that larval mushroom body output neurons, such as c2, f2, and m1, and larval dopaminergic neurons, such as DM1b, also connect these two brain regions. VFB holds [363](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003632,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central complex") records of neurons with some part in the adult central complex and [8](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=VFB_00050314,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in embryonic/larval lateral accessory lobe") records of neurons with some part in the embryonic/larval lateral accessory lobe, which may provide further insight into the connectivity between these regions. The strength of these connections is not specified in the available data.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as stated by Thomas and Wyman (1984). VFB records show that the giant fiber neuron has a distinct anatomy and connectivity. 

VFB holds [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") records of images of the giant fiber neuron, specifically DNp01, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01. The connectome data indicates that DNp01 has [361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream connectivity classes and [435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes. 

The giant fiber neuron is associated with certain GAL4 drivers, which have specific expression patterns. However, the exact details of these drivers are not specified in the provided evidence.

For further information, you can explore the available images of DNp01, transgene expression in DNp01, and downstream and upstream connectivity classes for DNp01, which are all available in VFB.

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response:
Based on the connectivity data, several neuron types might mediate a connection between the [visual system](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047735 "Open visual system in Virtual Fly Brain") and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"). The data indicates that neurons such as [ML-VPN2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052139 "Open ML-VPN2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052141 "Open Mt-VPN1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052140 "Open Mt-VPN in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mti](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052142 "Open Mti in Virtual Fly Brain"), and T4ai, which are associated with the visual system, could play a role in this connection. Additionally, neurons like [CB2311](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20005873 "Open CB2311 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [CB2443](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20005995 "Open CB2443 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [CB3379](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20006842 "Open CB3379 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [MB-C2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100228 "Open MB-C2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [MB-M1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100229 "Open MB-M1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), which are associated with the mushroom body, might also be involved. Furthermore, adult visual projection neurons are reported to have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, suggesting they could mediate the connection between the visual system and the mushroom body.

VFB holds a substantial amount of data on both the visual system and the mushroom body, including records of neurons with parts in or synaptic terminals in these systems. For the visual system, VFB has annotated [1046](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047735,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in visual system") neurons with some part in the visual system, as well as records of neurons with synaptic, presynaptic, and postsynaptic terminals in the visual system. For the mushroom body, VFB has annotated [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and also has records of neurons with synaptic, presynaptic, and postsynaptic terminals in the mushroom body.

The connectome data suggests that visual information could indeed reach the memory circuit via these neuron types, potentially facilitating the integration of visual information into memory processes. However, the exact nature and extent of this connection would require further examination of the available data and potentially additional evidence.

results.title: Comparative analysis
results.question: Compare the downstream targets of the two main types of clock neurons (s-LNv and l-LNv). Do they converge on any common target neuron types?
results.response: The downstream targets of [s-LNv](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch03yp "Open s-LNv in Virtual Fly Brain") and [l-LNv](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fws "Open l-LNv in Virtual Fly Brain") include several neuron types. According to VFB, comparing the downstream targets of s-LNv and l-LNv reveals 17 shared downstream target classes. These common target neuron types include adult interneuron, adult cholinergic neuron, adult GABAergic neuron, adult glutamatergic neuron, adult octopaminergic neuron, adult dopaminergic neuron, and adult serotonergic neuron. VFB holds data on these shared downstream targets, indicating that the s-LNv and l-LNv converge on these common target neuron types. To further explore the connectivity of these neuron types, you can query VFB for more specific information on the downstream targets of s-LNv and l-LNv.

results.title: Data availability survey
results.question: I'm interested in studying the subesophageal zone (SEZ). How well-characterised is this region in VFB? What neuron types are annotated, what connectomics data is available, and what genetic tools exist for SEZ neurons?
results.response:
The subesophageal zone (SEZ) is characterised in VFB with annotated neuron types. VFB records show the [larval subesophageal zone descending SEZ DN neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111241 "Open larval subesophageal zone descending SEZ DN neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is one of the neuron types annotated. The SEZ region in VFB is also described with specific neuron types annotated, such as larval neurons with their soma located at the level of the subesophageal zone, as noted by Ohyama et al., 2015. 

VFB holds connectomics data for the SEZ, including 95 upstream class-connectivity partners for the larval subesophageal zone vine neuron. 

For genetic tools, VFB has annotated 4205 genetic tool/expression pattern rows for the subesophageal zone, which include GAL4 drivers and binary/intersectional drivers. 

To further explore the SEZ, you can query VFB for more information on neuron types, connectomics data, and genetic tools.
